answer: PoA trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, causing influence to decay with distance and mixing constraints. A sybil coalition forms a sparse external cut S with low conductance, φ(S)=cut(S,V\S)/vol(S). Conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds limit the walk mass crossing into S, thereby bounding its aggregate voting weight regardless of its internal identity count; sable, summit, and ferrous attestations cannot amplify an isolated cluster past the honest boundary.
